newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank -- no key rate cut regardless of Buba.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank -- no key rate cut regardless of Buba.

text.p: Bank of Finland director Matti Vanhala said on Monday the central bank did not intend to cut its key tender rate soon, regardless of whether the German Bundesbank cut its key rates this week.

"If one looks at it (a key rate cut) for us, it would fit rather poorly with the economic forecasts we have ... in the situation that we have it does not sound like a good recipe," Vanhala told Reuters in a second telephone interview.
"On the contrary, it looks like something one could exclude," he said, adding he would find it "highly unlikely to even consider" a rate cut even if German rates changed.

Vanhala said the Bank of Finland saw no reason to raise the tender rate -- its key monetary policy tool -- either. The rate has been at 3.00 percent, on a par with the German repo rate, since last October.
Addressing the steep strengthening of the Finnish markka on Monday, Vanhala said the central bank had adopted a more liberal approach in foreign exchange intervention than last week.
But he declined to say whether the Bank of Finland had intervened at all on Monday to halt gains.
"The difference between last week and today is that our intervention policy has been slightly different," he said.
"Our approach today has been slightly more liberal," he added.
In general, the central bank's ambition was to have a "very stable currency" fluctuating "very close to the mid-point" in Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM), Vanhala said.

But from time to time, capital flows could increase pressures either way on the markka. "The broader +/-15 percent ERM band is, of course, at our disposal if the capital flows are big and the pressure strong," he said.
Recent flows of funds into the markka had "no longer been reasonable and moderate," Vanhala said.
